correctness.rationale: Every subset sum is a simplex prefix, so a putative radius below 1/√2 forces all nonzero subset sums to have squared length below two. Complete classification of short BCC vectors eliminates unit-coordinate-containing independent frames, and the half-diagonal sign-pair condition confines all remaining frames to one parity class. The Gram/centroid identity gives squared radius 5/16 exactly; explicit six-ordering centers give the sharp second threshold 1/2 in squared radius. A standard-library exact rational checker independently checks 232 independent triples using all short vectors, while infinite validity is proved analytically.

value.rationale: The recent six-simplex covering principle makes the worst minimum-ball radius over a common lattice frame a natural explicit geometric certificate. Proving an isolated global minimum, complete 48-ordered-frame rigidity and a sharp first attainable deterioration by factor √(8/5) is meaningful structural information for discrete lattice-frame covering and meshing, beyond the classical single BCC covering-radius value.
